title: Resources | Joel Polanco
description: Tools, templates, book recommendations, podcast recommendations
ogDescription: Tools, templates, book recommendations, podcast recommendations

items.title: Lenny's Newsletter & Podcast
items.description: My favorite product management resource. A paid subscription gets you access to the Slack community.

items.title: Reforge: Product & Growth Training
items.description: Reforge provides training targeted for mid-career product and growth professionals. I took courses in 2021.

items.title: Nikhyl Singhal: The Skip Podcast
items.description: My favorite career podcast. Nikhyl is a former VP of product with a superpower for coaching PMs/Execs.

items.title: Shreyas' Managing your PM Career
items.description: Shreyas Doshi is a legend in the product community. His 20 years of experience is unparalleled.

items.title: General Assembly: Product Training
items.description: I recommend General Assembly's product management course for early career professionals.

items.title: Paul Merriman Website & Newsletter
items.description: Paul Merriman is a retired financial advisor who advocates for factor-based DIY Index Fund Portfolios.

items.title: Never Search Alone Job Councils
items.description: Instead of "spray and pray" join one of Phyl Terry's job councils and find your candidate-market fit.

items.title: FS Blog & Knowledge Project Podcast
items.description: A newsletter and podcast produced by Shane Parrish. It is my go to for improving my decision-making.

items.title: Product-Market Fit Scale
items.description: My favorite depiction of what it means to have product-market fit over the life of a startup

items.title: Business Model Canvas Overview
items.description: This overview from Alex Cowan will show you what a business model canvas is and how to fill it out.

items.title: Inspired
items.description: My top recommended reading on what product management is. Written by Marty Cagan, a legend.

items.title: Good Strategy, Bad Strategy
items.description: This book is the authority on strategy. The author breaks down good and bad ones with examples.

items.title: Crossing the Chasm
items.description: A must read for anyone in product or marketing. It highlights the importance of market segmentation.

items.title: The Minimalist Entrepreneur
items.description: I like this author's backstory and his simple way of breaking down how to start a business.

items.title: Cracking the PM Interview
items.description: Read this book if you are interviewing for a product management role. The examples a bit dated but still apply.

items.title: The Cold Start Problem
items.description: The best book I've read on growing a network effects business. If you are trying to start a community, read it.

items.title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
items.description: "Spend each day trying to be a little wiser than you were when you woke up." This book will help you do that.

items.title: The E-Myth Revisited
items.description: This book did a great job breaking down the misconceptions of starting a business.

items.title: How will you measure your life?
items.description: I recommend this book to individuals who plan their careers without taking their personal life into account.

items.title: The score takes care of itself
items.description: This book shifted my focus from being solely "outcome over outputs" to "inputs achieve outcomes"

items.title: The Psychology of Money
items.description: My favorite book on personal finance. It highlights how to make better decisions with your money.

items.title: Influence
items.description: This book is the authority on ethical influence and persuasion. You will learn the universal principles.
